v1: Every move-out, working lamps and chargers go in the dumpster, while someone down the hall buys the same thing. Most listings stop at posted.
v3: It starts with a need, not a sale. Someone on campus asks for a reading lamp. That is all Loop knows about them.
v4: The giver posts a photo. Gemini drafts the listing, and notices who asked for exactly this. It only drafts. The giver fixes the condition, and offers it.
v6: The taker accepts, and leaves the pickup blank on purpose. They have never met, and will never know each other's names.
v7: Now Loop is the third voice in the chat. It asks the giver first, because the giver is doing the favour. A tap becomes a proposal, the other side confirms, and Loop reminds both later. It proposes. It never decides.
v8: At the library, the taker shows four digits, and the giver types them. That is the whole handshake.
v9: And if you never open the app, text a photo to Loop. Same draft, same honesty. Every question ends with a thumbs-up or thumbs-down you can tap.
v10: The honest parts are the point. One photo becomes six drafts. Gemini says when nothing fits, and Loop says no when it should.
v11: Node and plain JavaScript, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite behind JSON schemas, and Photon Spectrum for iMessage.
